## Purpose

Repair a stale checkpoint on an already COMPLETED Git-first container using its
accepted, published final pass source. Preview is the default. Apply requires
the exact preview identities and an audit reason. See the
[design and operator procedure](../../specs/design/completed-container-checkpoint-recovery.md).

## When a playbook uses it

An authorized integration recovery workflow may call this after identifying a
historical completed container whose checkpoint still names its old base.
The caller must be the local operator, a live named supervisor for the project,
or an operator worker carrying the existing scoped integration authority grant.
The ordinary worker profile cannot perform this recovery.

## How it works internally

The CommandHandler validates arguments and integration recovery authority, then
[`CompletedContainerRecovery`](../../../src/integration/completed_container_recovery.py)
snapshots the task, completion, children, checkpoint, origin and branch owner.
It verifies the canonical repository, exact authenticated remote head and Git
ancestry. Under the repository transaction, completion-table lock, branch owner
lock and hierarchy lock, it rechecks the snapshot, remote and caller authority.
Apply compares and swaps only the checkpoint provenance and writes its receipt
in the same database transaction.

## Side effects and persistence

Preview writes no database state. Git proof may fetch the ordinary retained
object cache. Apply updates `task_integration_checkpoints.checkpoint_sha`,
`version` and `updated_at`, preserving generation and all other checkpoint data.
It inserts one durable `integration.completed_container_checkpoint_recovered`
event with attributable before/after proof. An identical repeat verifies the
current proof and returns the same receipt without writing again. Completion,
task, child, origin, ownership, remote ref and delivery target remain untouched.

## Failure modes and diagnostics

`invalid` identifies missing apply pins or malformed arguments. `refused`
reports changed or missing identities, unresolved children, nonpassing or
unpublished provenance, an active writer/episode/handoff, inactive Git-first, or
changed authority. The CLI allows the preview or apply 300 seconds to answer,
because the Git proof includes a retained fetch; a reply lost past that bound
reports `outcome: unknown` and is never retried automatically, so rerun the
read-only preview before any apply. A fresh CLI preview provides the current
diagnostic; investigate changed provenance before applying. Recovery does not
satisfy exact-source review, hosted CI or normal train delivery gates.

## Example step

An authorized supervisor can begin with a native preview:

```bash
aq integration recover-completed-container container-1 \
  --project proj-1 --repository repo-1 --branch aq/container-1 --json
```

Use the native operator procedure linked above to inspect the result and supply
all preview pins for an explicit apply.
